_doc: Stream E (M2b). Broadly tagged vignettes (5-7 archetypes, 4+ biomes each) added so tools/assign-vignettes.mjs can meet the variety rule (any 5 connected zones >= 40 distinct), plus 4 quest-specific ones (fen_witch_hut, tinker_wagon, hunters_hide, cult_cellar) that keep M2 quests off the M1 starter vignettes (no vignette twice within 2 zones). Same format as m1.json.

vignettes.name: The Salt Cart
vignettes.blurb: A salt merchant's cart sunk axle-deep in soft ground; crabs and croakers fight over the spill.
vignettes.lore: The cart sank slowly. You can tell, because the driver had time to write HELP on the side in salt.

objects.name: Salt-written plea
objects.text: HELP. ALSO TELL MOTHER THE SALT WAS NOT MY FAULT.

vignettes.name: The Lime Cairn
vignettes.blurb: A cairn of chalk-white stones over an old sickness pit; rats nest in it and the grass refuses to grow.
vignettes.lore: Nobody can recall what killed them. The lime on the stones says somebody wanted it to stay buried.

objects.name: Loose cairn stone
objects.text: Under the stone: three old coins and a smell you will not forget for a week.

vignettes.name: The Drowned Belfry
vignettes.blurb: Only the top of a bell tower shows above a mere; on still nights the bell rings by itself. Wisps gather.
vignettes.lore: The church is under the water. The bell is not. It rings when the wind is not blowing, which is the worrying part.

objects.name: Bell rope
objects.text: You pull. Somewhere under your feet, something answers.

vignettes.name: The Tithe Barn
vignettes.blurb: A church tithe barn whose roof fell in on the harvest; boars got in through the gap and refuse to leave.
vignettes.lore: The tithe was a tenth of everything. The boars have taken the other nine tenths personally.

vignettes.name: The Slag Saint
vignettes.blurb: A heap of mine slag with a crude face carved into it and candles at its foot; miners swear it brings luck. Beetles live inside.
vignettes.lore: Somebody carved a face into the slag heap and gave it a little hat. Somebody else has been leaving it beer.

objects.name: Beer cup at the saint's feet
objects.text: You leave a coin. The slag saint seems to wink.

vignettes.name: The Tide Post
vignettes.blurb: A tall post on the shore hung with bells that ring when the tide turns; a drowned fisherman's tally carved down it. Serpents in the shallows.
vignettes.lore: Somebody counted the tides on this post for forty years. The last notch is very deep, as if he pressed hard.

objects.name: The tally post
objects.text: Forty years of notches. The last one says, in tiny letters: 'It came up with the tide. It was smiling.'

vignettes.name: The Spider Bridge
vignettes.blurb: An old rope bridge over a gully, its ropes thick with spider silk; the toll box is still there, full.
vignettes.lore: The bridge is held together mostly by webbing now. The toll box says 'One copper'. The spiders seem to have collected it.

vignettes.name: The Burnt Choir
vignettes.blurb: Six charred standing stones in a ring, each shaped vaguely like a singer; the ground between them is warm. Ash wisps drift.
vignettes.lore: The stones are warm to the touch and arranged like a choir. If you hum, the ashes on the ground shiver.

objects.name: Warm altar stone
objects.text: You hum a note. The stones hum it back, and something about you feels tougher.

vignettes.name: The Guildhall Shell
vignettes.blurb: The shell of a craft guild's hall, its sign still hanging by one chain; brigands use it as a counting house.
vignettes.lore: The sign says 'Worshipful Company of Lampwrights'. The brigands inside are worshipping mostly coins.

objects.name: Ledger page
objects.text: Paid: 3 silver for 'protection'. Paid: 3 silver for protection from the protection.

vignettes.name: The Sinkhole Garden
vignettes.blurb: A neat round sinkhole with a perfect little garden at the bottom and no way down except jumping; mushroom folk tend it.
vignettes.lore: Somebody has planted cabbages at the bottom of a sinkhole. In rows. With a scarecrow. Nobody knows how they get down.

objects.name: Prize cabbage
objects.text: The biggest cabbage you have ever seen. It would be a shame to leave it.

vignettes.name: The Heretic's Stake
vignettes.blurb: A charred stake on a hill with a ring of stones around it and a sign forbidding all approach; the ash never blows away. Wraith-light at night.
vignettes.lore: A sign says KEEP AWAY in three languages and one drawing. The drawing is the most convincing.

objects.name: Charred confession
objects.text: I only said the abbot snored. — Halbert

vignettes.name: The Old Pump House
vignettes.blurb: A brick pump house that drained the lowland, its wheel jammed by a nest of slimes; turning it back on floods the next field.
vignettes.lore: The great wheel has stopped. Something green has been keeping it stopped, apparently on purpose.

objects.name: Jammed pump wheel
objects.text: You heave. The wheel groans round, and a field away somebody shouts in delight.

vignettes.name: The False Beacon
vignettes.blurb: A beacon fire on a headland set to lure ships onto the rocks, still laid and ready; the wreckers left in a hurry.
vignettes.lore: The fire is laid and the oil is fresh. Real lighthouses do not hide behind gorse bushes.

objects.name: Kick the beacon apart
objects.text: You scatter the firewood. Somewhere out at sea, a ship you will never meet does not sink.

vignettes.name: The Bone Orchard
vignettes.blurb: Apple trees in a walled churchyard, fat with fruit nobody dares pick; their roots go into the graves. Barrow hounds patrol.
vignettes.lore: The apples are the reddest in the province. The villagers will not touch them, and will not say why.

objects.name: Red apple
objects.text: It tastes wonderful. You try very hard not to think about the roots.

vignettes.name: The Lock-Keeper's Cottage
vignettes.blurb: A canal lock with a tidy cottage; the lock-keeper is gone but his supper is still warm. Something croaks in the lock.
vignettes.lore: The kettle is warm. The supper is half eaten. The lock gates are open and the water below is very, very dark.

objects.name: Lock-keeper's diary
objects.text: Day 12. The big one is back in the lock. I have named him Gerald. Gerald does not like me.

vignettes.name: The Drift Entry
vignettes.blurb: A small drift mine cut into a bank, its props rotten and its tally board half-filled; the last shift left their lamps.
vignettes.lore: Twelve names on the tally board. Eleven lamps on the hooks. Nobody wants to count again.

objects.name: Shift tally board
objects.text: Twelve marks for twelve men in. Eleven marks out. Someone has scratched a twelfth, much later, in a shaky hand.

vignettes.name: The Warden's Cairn
vignettes.blurb: A big cairn on a rise where border wardens leave a stone for each patrol; a deserter's pack is hidden in it. Hyenas scavenge.
vignettes.lore: Every warden who passes adds a stone. One stone has been taken out, and a pack stuffed in the hole.

objects.name: Deserter's pack
objects.hint: One stone near the bottom is newer than the rest.

vignettes.name: The Mudlark Flats
vignettes.blurb: Tidal mudflats where children dig for lost treasures at low tide; today the mud is digging back. Silt lurkers.
vignettes.lore: The mudlarks say you can find anything in the flats if you dig long enough. Today the flats found them first.

objects.name: Pip the mudlark
says: Don't step there! That's where the mud bites.
Find me a silver spoon and I'll tell you where the old king's ring went.

vignettes.name: The Broken Aqueduct
vignettes.blurb: Three arches of an old aqueduct striding across nothing; water still trickles from the broken end into a pool. Wisps and moths.
vignettes.lore: The aqueduct carried water from somewhere to somewhere else. Both somewheres are gone. The water did not get the message.

objects.name: Trickling spout
objects.text: The water is cold and tastes faintly of old stone. You feel better.

vignettes.name: The Crow Cage
vignettes.blurb: An iron cage hung from a tree by the road with a skeleton in it that someone has dressed in a fresh hat; crows and owls.
vignettes.lore: The skeleton is very old. The hat is very new. There is a note pinned to the hat.

objects.name: Note on the hat
objects.text: He looked cold. — the people of the next village, who are nicer than ours

vignettes.name: The Tar Seep
vignettes.blurb: Bubbling black pits where tar rises from the ground; old bones and a lost horse cart are half sunk. Something slick moves underneath.
vignettes.lore: The tar takes everything slowly. A cart, a horse, a very surprised deer. It is in no hurry with you either.

vignettes.name: The Abandoned Fish Stall
vignettes.blurb: A market fish stall left mid-sale, fish still on the slab and the scales still balanced; cats and rats feud over it.
vignettes.lore: The scales are perfectly balanced: one fish against one gold coin. Nobody has dared to touch either.

objects.name: The balanced scales
objects.text: You take the coin. The fish, oddly, looks relieved.

vignettes.name: The Footbath of Saint Ida
vignettes.blurb: A stone trough where pilgrims wash their feet; the water is said to cure blisters and cowardice. A cult has fouled it.
vignettes.lore: Saint Ida cured blisters. The men camped around her trough are mostly curing their boredom by shouting at you.

objects.name: Saint Ida's trough
objects.text: Your feet feel brand new. So, briefly, does your courage.

vignettes.name: The Quarry Crane
vignettes.blurb: A wooden crane over a flooded quarry with a block of marble still hanging from it; turning the windlass drops it on whatever lives in the water.
vignettes.lore: The block has hung there for twenty years. The rope has been patient. The rope is nearly out of patience.

objects.name: Windlass
objects.text: The block drops into the water with a tremendous noise. Something underneath stops moving.

vignettes.name: The Great Skull
vignettes.blurb: A skull the size of a cottage half-buried in a hillside, its eye sockets used as a shelter by shepherds and now by something hungrier.
vignettes.lore: Shepherds used to sleep in the eye socket. They say you dream of flying. The current tenants dream of shepherds.

objects.name: Shepherd's stash in the eye socket

vignettes.name: The Ferryman's Coin
vignettes.blurb: A tiny shrine at a river crossing where travellers leave a coin for safe passage; the coins are untouched for a hundred years. Wraiths guard it.
vignettes.lore: A hundred years of coins, and not one stolen. Either the folk here are very honest, or something keeps count.

objects.name: Offering bowl
objects.text: You leave a coin. A cold hand pats yours, approvingly.

vignettes.name: Old Mabry's Stilt Hut
vignettes.blurb: Brackwater's hedge-witch lives in a hut on stilts at the edge of the reeds; her slime jars have tipped over and the slimes are loose in the shallows. Quest NPC Old Mabry stands here (brackwater).
vignettes.lore: A hut on four crooked legs, a ladder, a shelf of jars. Several of the jars are empty and wobbling away.

objects.name: Label on an empty jar
objects.text: SLIME (GREEN). DO NOT OPEN. Mabry, this means you.

vignettes.name: The Tinker's Wagon
vignettes.blurb: A tinker's painted wagon pulled off the road with a broken axle; rats have got into the stock. Quest NPC Cadoc the tinker stands here (millbrook).
vignettes.lore: Pots hang from every hook of a painted wagon. One wheel is off. So, judging by the squeaking, is the lid of the cheese box.

objects.name: Grindstone
objects.text: You give your blade a turn on the tinker's grindstone. It comes away sharper and so do you.

vignettes.name: The Hunter's Hide
vignettes.blurb: A brushwood hide above a churned boar wallow; the hunter lost his bow in the mud and his dog to the hounds. Quest NPC Hob the hunter waits here (wychwood).
vignettes.lore: A screen of cut branches, a stool, and below it a wallow churned to soup. A bowstring sticks up out of the mud like a question.

vignettes.name: The Cloud-Shouters' Cellar
vignettes.blurb: A burned frontier farm with a cellar where sky cultists meet to shout at the weather. Quest NPC Scout Tamsin watches it (redcliff).
vignettes.lore: The farmhouse is ash. The cellar door is new, and from under it comes a voice telling the clouds exactly what it thinks of them.

objects.name: Cellar door
objects.text: Behind the door: candles, a chalk circle and a list of grievances against the sky.
